findings.title: Spawned flusher processes are not killed before replacement
findings.body: `self.mp_context` is `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")`, so the entries in `self.processes` are `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess` objects. The top-level `multiprocessing.Process` is a different class on systems where the default context is not spawn, so `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` can be false for these spawned processes. In `_ensure_processes_alive`, a hung process is therefore not killed, but `_create_process_for_shards` still starts a replacement for the same shards. This leaves the old flusher alive and can cause two processes to flush/produce the same segments concurrently, leading to duplicate spans in Kafka. The same incorrect check in `join()` (line 346) also prevents spawned processes from being terminated on timeout. Check against `self.mp_context.Process` or `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess` instead.

findings.title: join() skips termination of remaining processes once timeout expires
findings.body: In `join`, the loop checks `remaining_time <= 0` and then `break`s out of the entire process loop. If `next_step.join(timeout)` or waiting for an earlier flusher process consumes the whole deadline, later flusher processes are never waited on and never reach `process.terminate()`. Because `stopped` only requests a graceful shutdown, a stuck child can keep running after `join()` returns, leaking resources or continuing to produce during shutdown/rebalance. The loop should still terminate all remaining processes after the deadline expires, or calculate per-process timeouts differently.

findings.title: Multi-process flusher test only checks process mapping, not flushing behavior
findings.body: `test_flusher_processes_limit` verifies that `SpanFlusher` creates the expected number of processes and distributes shards, but it never submits spans, polls the pipeline, or asserts produced Kafka payloads. The actual behavior of multiple flusher processes sharing shards—flushing segments from Redis, producing to Kafka, and completing `done_flush_segments`—is not exercised, so a regression in the multiprocess flushing path would not be caught by this test. Add a functional test with spans on multiple partitions and assert the produced messages.
